# Results — Study 417 (Island Reversal)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a cluster of
bars marooned between two opposite gaps marks an exhausted trend; short the island top (and buy the
island bottom) when the second gap seals it** — tested with an **objective, mechanical** detector
on daily OHLC. Chart figures are partly subjective, so we test the closest rules-based definition
(a clear gap in one direction, a 1–3-bar island that never fills it, then a sealing gap of the same
size in the opposite direction that re-isolates it) and say so. For each confirmed island we
measure the forward **5 / 10 / 20 / 40-day** return in the figure's intended direction, **net of
each name's own base rate**, with a 1-day entry lag. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted** (split + dividend) OHLC — SPY + 29 long-listed US large-caps (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last bar **2026-05-29**; no partial month in the stamped run) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**21.4** years; **5,385** daily bars) |
| Panel | **30** names · fingerprint **`bcc8dc7157c7`** |
| Detector | gap threshold **1%**; island 1–3 bars whose range never fills the first gap; sealing gap = first opposite gap that re-crosses the island's far edge *and* opens back inside the pre-gap range; non-overlapping |
| Islands | **75** confirmed island-**tops** (SPY: 3) · **97** island-**bottoms** (myth-check, SPY: 3) |
| Timing / costs | enter the close **1 day after** the sealing gap (no look-ahead); hold 5/10/20/40 days; **5 bps** one-way × 2 legs |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026. A
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include names that delisted after a failed reversal, which
> tilts post-island forward returns mildly **up** — i.e. *against* the bearish island-top short
> (the headline) and mildly *for* the bullish island-bottom. The headline (bearish) read is, if
> anything, fighting a tailwind — and it still fails.

> **Gap-on-adjusted-tape caveat.** Auto-adjustment back-applies split/dividend factors, so the
> *gap* the detector sees is the gap a present-day analyst reconstructs from the adjusted series,
> not necessarily the raw tick of the day. This is the same convention as the rest of the bench's
> pattern studies; the conclusion (no edge) is robust across the gap-threshold sweep.

## The signal — island-top (bearish, SHORT) forward edge, EXCESS over base rate

The excess pools every confirmed island top across the basket, subtracting each name's own
unconditional mean forward return (the short's base rate = −buy-and-hold) so the test is "does the
figure beat shorting *that name* at random", not "is the market down". *t* is one-sample; HAC *t*
is Newey-West; the placebo *p* is the share of **5,000 random-date entries** on the same tape whose
pooled excess **beats** the observed one.

| horizon | n | excess | raw | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 75 | **−0.705%** | −1.025% | 45% | −1.27 | −1.21 | 0.641 | −0.805% |
| 10-day | 75 | **−1.275%** | −1.906% | 39% | −1.59 | −1.36 | 0.678 | −1.375% |
| 20-day | 75 | −0.640% | −1.901% | 45% | −0.55 | −0.49 | 0.562 | −0.740% |
| 40-day | 73 | −0.336% | −2.794% | 49% | −0.22 | −0.20 | 0.524 | −0.436% |

Read it carefully. The headline figure — the **island top**, the one chartists draw and call a
high-confidence reversal — produces a short excess that is **negative at every horizon**. The
*t* is negative throughout (best magnitude −1.59 at 10 days), nowhere near the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar,
and the placebo it cannot beat (random short dates do *better* ~52–68% of the time). The negative
excess means the figure-following short reliably **underperforms a random short**: the names keep
drifting *up* after the supposedly bearish island, exactly the wrong direction. There is no
exhaustion here — only a shape the market ignores.

## Robustness — no gap threshold rescues the island top

If the figure were real, demanding a *cleaner* island (a bigger sealing gap) should *sharpen* it.
It doesn't — the short excess stays negative and the *t* never approaches +2 at any strictness.

| gap threshold | n (10-day) | excess (10-day) | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.5% | 198 | −0.551% | −1.31 | 0.616 |
| **1.0%** | **75** | **−1.275%** | **−1.59** | **0.673** |
| 2.0% | 17 | −0.989% | −0.53 | 0.598 |

The strictest setting collapses to **17 events** (the mechanical island is genuinely rare on liquid
large-caps), and the loosest (n = 198) is still negative at *t* = −1.31. There is no gap size at
which "two gaps bracketing a cluster" becomes a tradable reversal.

## Myth check — the island BOTTOM only rides the tape's up-drift

A genuine reversal figure should work on **both** sides. We run the identical machinery on the
**island bottom** (gap down, cluster at the low, sealing gap up) as a **long**, measuring the
long's excess over a long's base rate.

| horizon | n | long excess | raw | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 97 | +0.762% | +1.085% | 60% | +1.77 | +1.74 | 0.337 |
| 10-day | 96 | +0.328% | +0.965% | 49% | +0.48 | +0.51 | 0.454 |
| 20-day | 96 | **+2.022%** | +3.294% | 59% | +2.04 | +2.40 | 0.292 |
| 40-day | 94 | **+5.284%** | +7.762% | 69% | +4.22 | +4.29 | 0.163 |

This is the trap that fools the eye. The island-bottom long shows a big positive excess that *grows*
with horizon and a one-sample *t* that clears 2 at 20–40 days — looks like a real bullish reversal.
But the **placebo refuses it**: even at 40 days, random long entries on the same tape beat the
observed mean **16%** of the time (*p* = 0.163), never dropping below the 5% line. The high *t* is
manufactured by the basket's strong multi-week **up-drift** compounding over the hold — not by the
figure. The asymmetry is the diagnosis: the bullish side only *looks* alive because it borrows the
market's drift, and the bearish side, which must fight that drift, drowns. The figure is not reading
exhaustion at all.

## SPY-only — does the island top beat SPY? (the README hook)

| horizon | n | excess | raw | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 3 | −1.300% | −1.537% | −0.73 | 0.860 |
| 10-day | 3 | −0.907% | −1.376% | −1.37 | 0.699 |
| 20-day | 3 | −1.067% | −2.004% | −0.47 | 0.654 |
| 40-day | 3 | −5.150% | −6.997% | −1.81 | 0.946 |

On the index itself the detector fires only **3** times in 21 years — far too few to say anything —
and every excess is negative with a placebo near or above 0.7. The "short the SPY island top" recipe
is a non-event.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel with *planted* island tops followed by a real **down** reversal, the
same-tape placebo behaves exactly as it must.

| planted edge | planted | detected | n | excess (20-day) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 160 | 158 | 158 | −0.58% | −1.50 | **0.627** | 47% |
| **+0.25** (large planted reversal) | 160 | 158 | 158 | **+18.33%** | **+59.38** | **0.000** | 100% |

With **no** planted reversal the placebo is **not beaten** (p = 0.63 — no false positive); a large
planted reversal lights up at p = 0.000, *t* = +59, win 100%. The harness can clearly bank a real
edge — so the real-tape placebo *p* ≈ 0.56–0.68 on the island top is a genuine **nothing**, not a
power failure.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The island-top short excess is **negative at every horizon** (−0.71% at 5d,
  −1.28% at 10d), with a one-sample *t* that never exceeds −1.6 in magnitude (HAC the same) and a
  placebo it cannot beat (*p* = 0.52–0.68) — and survivorship tilts *against* the short, so this is
  if anything generous. Indistinguishable from noise; the figure does not mark exhaustion.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 5 bps/leg the island-top short is **−0.81% to −1.38%** across
  horizons (worse than random), and the island-bottom long's apparent edge sits **inside the placebo
  cloud** (p ≥ 0.16) — pure beta, not alpha. No deployable edge, nothing to scale.
- **"Reliable reversal"? — BUSTED.** The two sides are asymmetric: the bearish island top **loses**
  (negative excess, fights the up-drift) while the bullish island bottom only **rides market drift**
  (high *t* but a placebo it can't beat). A real reversal figure would work on both sides on its own
  merits; this one works on neither. "A cluster marooned by two gaps" is a shape the eye finds, not a
  force the tape obeys.
